items.title: A bag line without a message offers "Add a gift message" and shows no message
covers: AC1: line has an "Add a gift message" action
AC1: a line without a message otherwise looks as today
items.reason: AC1 is the entry point of the feature and promises that a line without a message is otherwise unchanged; if the action is missing nothing else can be reached, and a stray quoted text or "Edit" on an empty line would be a visible regression. Only the rendered `/cart` page proves this, so e2e.

items.title: Saving a gift message shows it in quotes under the product name with an "Edit" action
covers: AC2: message shown under the product name, in quotes
AC2: "Edit" action replaces "Add a gift message"
items.reason: AC2 is the core happy path: write, save, see it. It is a full browser round trip (form post on the static SSR page, Basket API write, re-render), so only e2e exercises it end to end.

items.title: The message box stops at 60 characters and a 60-character message is saved whole
covers: AC6: the box does not let me type more than 60 characters
AC2: message of up to 60 characters
items.reason: AC6 is the only stated limit and it is a property of the box in the browser; the boundary is checked just outside (61 typed) and exactly at the limit (60 kept and saved), so a shopper's longest allowed message is not truncated or refused. Only a real browser enforces typing limits, so e2e.

items.title: Editing a gift message replaces the shown message
covers: AC3: edit and save shows the new message
items.reason: AC3 lets the shopper change the message until checkout; the edit path pre-fills and overwrites a stored value, a different code path from the first save, so it gets its own case. Browser flow, so e2e.

items.title: Clearing the text and saving removes the message and brings back "Add a gift message"
covers: AC3: clearing the text and saving removes the message
AC3: "Add a gift message" shown again
items.reason: AC3 makes an empty save the way to remove a message; if it stored an empty string the line would show `""` or keep "Edit". It is checked after a reload too, so the removal is proven on the server, not only in the rendered response. Browser flow, so e2e.

items.title: The gift message survives a page reload
covers: AC4: message still there after reloading the page
items.reason: AC4 requires the message to be stored, not just rendered once; a reload re-reads the basket from the Basket API. Kept separate from sign-out and quantity changes because each one rebuilds the basket through a different path.

items.title: The gift message survives signing out and signing in again
covers: AC4: message still there after sign out and sign in
Implementation Notes: message lives with the basket on the server, not in the browser
items.reason: AC4 and the notes require the message to live with the server-side basket; signing in from a fresh browser context proves nothing is kept in browser storage or the session. Needs Identity and the WebApp, so e2e.

items.title: The gift message survives a change of the line's quantity
covers: AC4: message still there after changing the line's quantity
items.reason: A quantity update rewrites the whole basket through the Basket API; if the WebApp sent the items without their messages, the message would be lost silently. AC4 names this action explicitly, and it crosses the WebApp and the API, so e2e.

items.title: Removing the product and adding it again from its product page gives a line with no message
covers: AC5: removing the product and adding it again gives a line with no message
items.reason: AC5 says the message belongs to the line, not the product: a re-added product must not inherit the old message (for example from a cache or a leftover record). The flow spans the bag and the product page, so e2e.

items.title: Placing an order from a bag with a gift message still creates the order
covers: Implementation Notes: placing an order is unchanged
items.reason: The notes require checkout to stay unchanged; a new field on the basket item could break the order request the WebApp builds from the bag. A created order is only reachable on the test stack (the Ordering functional host cannot save one), so e2e.

items.title: Redis keeps a basket item's gift message across save and load
covers: AC4: message persisted with the basket
Implementation Notes: message lives with the basket on the server
items.reason: AC4 depends on the message being written to and read from Redis with the basket; a missing serializer property (source-generated `BasketSerializationContext`) would drop it silently. Real Redis serialization is only exercised by the functional fixture, so functional rather than unit.

items.title: A basket stored without any gift message field still loads from Redis
covers: AC7: a bag saved before this change still opens
Implementation Notes: a stored basket without messages still loads
items.reason: AC7 protects every shopper's existing bag: baskets in Redis were serialized before `GiftMessage` existed. A deserialization failure would make the bag unopenable. The stored shape can only be written directly to Redis, which the functional fixture allows and the test stack scenarios do not.

items.title: GetBasket returns an empty gift_message for a stored item without a message
covers: AC7: lines of an old bag show "Add a gift message"
Outputs: BasketItem.gift_message (proto field 7)
items.reason: AC7's display depends on the API turning a null stored message into the proto default (`""`), which the WebApp reads as "no message"; assigning null to a protobuf string field throws, which would break every old bag. Pure mapping with a mocked repository, so unit.

items.title: UpdateBasket accepts an item sent without gift_message and stores no message
covers: Implementation Notes: an item sent without a message is accepted
items.reason: The notes require existing Basket API callers (which never set field 7) to keep working; such an item must be stored as "no message", not as an empty string or an error. Request mapping with a mocked repository, so unit.

items.title: UpdateBasket stores and returns a 60-character gift message unchanged
covers: AC2: message of up to 60 characters
AC4: message stored with the basket
items.reason: AC2 allows messages up to 60 characters, so the API must accept the limit exactly, without truncating or refusing it (an off-by-one in a server-side check would break the longest message the box lets through). Pure request mapping, so unit.

items.title: UpdateBasket with an empty gift_message on an item that had one stores no message
covers: AC3: clearing the text removes the message
Implementation Notes: message lives on the server
items.reason: AC3's clear is carried to the server as an empty `gift_message`; the API must replace the stored message with "no message" rather than keep the old one. Proven at the service boundary with a mocked repository so the stored value can be asserted exactly; the visible result is covered by TC-GIFT-1-05.

items.reason: AC3 lets the shopper change the message until checkout; the edit path pre-fills and overwrites a stored value, a different code path from the first save, so it gets its own case. Browser flow, so e2e.

items.title: Clearing the text and saving removes the message and brings back "Add a gift message"
covers: AC3: clearing the text and saving removes the message
AC3: "Add a gift message" shown again
items.reason: AC3 makes an empty save the way to remove a message; if it stored an empty string the line would show `""` or keep "Edit". It is checked after a reload too, so the removal is proven on the server, not only in the rendered response. Browser flow, so e2e.

items.title: The gift message survives a page reload
covers: AC4: message still there after reloading the page
items.reason: AC4 requires the message to be stored, not just rendered once; a reload re-reads the basket from the Basket API. Kept separate from sign-out and quantity changes because each one rebuilds the basket through a different path.

items.title: The gift message survives signing out and signing in again
covers: AC4: message still there after sign out and sign in
Implementation Notes: message lives with the basket on the server, not in the browser
items.reason: AC4 and the notes require the message to live with the server-side basket; signing in from a fresh browser context proves nothing is kept in browser storage or the session. Needs Identity and the WebApp, so e2e.

items.title: The gift message survives a change of the line's quantity
covers: AC4: message still there after changing the line's quantity
items.reason: A quantity update rewrites the whole basket through the Basket API; if the WebApp sent the items without their messages, the message would be lost silently. AC4 names this action explicitly, and it crosses the WebApp and the API, so e2e.

items.title: Removing the product and adding it again from its product page gives a line with no message
covers: AC5: removing the product and adding it again gives a line with no message
items.reason: AC5 says the message belongs to the line, not the product: a re-added product must not inherit the old message (for example from a cache or a leftover record). The flow spans the bag and the product page, so e2e.

items.title: Placing an order from a bag with a gift message still creates the order
covers: Implementation Notes: placing an order is unchanged
items.reason: The notes require checkout to stay unchanged; a new field on the basket item could break the order request the WebApp builds from the bag. A created order is only reachable on the test stack (the Ordering functional host cannot save one), so e2e.

items.title: Redis keeps a basket item's gift message across save and load
covers: AC4: message persisted with the basket
Implementation Notes: message lives with the basket on the server
items.reason: AC4 depends on the message being written to and read from Redis with the basket; a missing serializer property (source-generated `BasketSerializationContext`) would drop it silently. Real Redis serialization is only exercised by the functional fixture, so functional rather than unit.

items.title: A basket stored without any gift message field still loads from Redis
covers: AC7: a bag saved before this change still opens
Implementation Notes: a stored basket without messages still loads
items.reason: AC7 protects every shopper's existing bag: baskets in Redis were serialized before `GiftMessage` existed. A deserialization failure would make the bag unopenable. The stored shape can only be written directly to Redis, which the functional fixture allows and the test stack scenarios do not.

items.title: GetBasket returns an empty gift_message for a stored item without a message
covers: AC7: lines of an old bag show "Add a gift message"
Outputs: BasketItem.gift_message (proto field 7)
items.reason: AC7's display depends on the API turning a null stored message into the proto default (`""`), which the WebApp reads as "no message"; assigning null to a protobuf string field throws, which would break every old bag. Pure mapping with a mocked repository, so unit.

items.title: UpdateBasket accepts an item sent without gift_message and stores no message
covers: Implementation Notes: an item sent without a message is accepted
items.reason: The notes require existing Basket API callers (which never set field 7) to keep working; such an item must be stored as "no message", not as an empty string or an error. Request mapping with a mocked repository, so unit.

items.title: A rejected save keeps the stored message under the product name and shows an inline error
covers: AC3: the line shows the message it has until a save succeeds
Upheld finding SOL-1: a failed save keeps the stored message and shows an inline error
items.reason: Regression case for the upheld finding SOL-1: when the Basket API refuses a save, the line must keep showing the stored message (not the refused text) and tell the shopper inline, instead of failing the page or pretending the save worked. The only way to make a save fail from the browser is a message over 60 characters, which needs the box's `maxlength` removed in the DOM; the visible result and its persistence after reload are browser behaviour, so e2e.

items.title: A gift message post without a product id shows a notice above the bag and changes nothing
covers: Upheld finding SOL-2: a gift message post without a product id shows a notice above the bag and leaves the basket unchanged
items.reason: Regression case for the upheld finding SOL-2: a gift-message post that names no line (no `GiftMessageProductId`) must not change any line or fail the page; it shows a notice above the bag instead. The post can only be produced by removing the hidden input in the browser, and the notice is rendered markup, so e2e.

items.title: A gift message post without a product id on an empty bag shows the notice and the bag stays empty
covers: Upheld finding SOL-2: the missing-product notice is shown on an empty bag too
items.reason: SOL-2 was upheld again after the first fix because the notice was not rendered when the bag was empty (the empty-bag branch replaced the item list). This is a separate rendering path from TC-GIFT-1-18, so it gets its own case. The stale form is produced by emptying the bag in a second tab, which only a browser can do, so e2e.

items.title: The order request sent to Ordering carries no gift message
covers: Implementation Notes: placing an order is unchanged, the message is not sent to ordering
items.reason: The notes say the message is not sent to ordering. TC-GIFT-1-10 only proves checkout still succeeds, which Ordering would also do if it silently ignored a forwarded field. This case checks the actual outgoing JSON built by the production serialization (`OrderingService.CreateOrder` with `JsonContent.Create`), which needs no running service, so unit.
